--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.colorize_node_attrs()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Map node attribute values to colors. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.colorize_node_attrs()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Map node attribute values to colors. title: >- [Graph.colorize_node_attrs()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Map node attribute values to colors. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Map node attribute values to colors. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L27846-L28062){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.colorize_node_attrs( node_attr_from=None, values=None, node_attr_to="color", palette="default", alpha=None, nodes=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Colorize node attributes](../assets/graphs/colorize-node-attrs.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Before: a six-node graph whose nodes carry a community attribute, shown as badges with the values 0, 1, and 2. After: each node has a color written from its value, so the two nodes with 0 are in the accent color, the two with 1 in teal, and the two with 2 in violet." width="100%"} Turns a categorical node attribute (or a dict of values) into hex color strings and writes them to another node attribute, `color` by default, modifying the graph in place. The distinct values are sorted and each one is paired with the next color of the palette, so nodes sharing a value always share a color. If there are more distinct values than palette colors, the palette is recycled from the start, which means different values can end up with the same color. This is the usual way to make groups visible in a plot, for example: - coloring nodes by detected community (`cmty_louvain()` and friends) - distinguishing node types or categories (e.g., person vs. organization) - highlighting a status flag or any other discrete label The mapping is categorical: each distinct value gets its own palette entry, and no interpolation is performed between colors. For continuous measures such as centrality scores, consider bucketing the values first or using `rescale_node_attrs()` to map them to node sizes instead. The mapping is also recorded on the graph and listed under "Node aesthetics" by `describe()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [node_attr_from]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute to read values from (e.g., `"community"`, `"type"`). Nodes without this attribute are left uncolored. Ignored for reading when `values=` is given (it is then only used to label the recorded aesthetic). Default is `None`; either this or `values=` must be supplied. [values]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, Any]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A dict mapping nodes to the values to colorize, keyed by node ID (`int`) or label (`str`). Use this to color by data that isn't stored as an attribute, such as the output of a `return_dict=True` computation. If given, it takes precedence over `node_attr_from=` and `nodes=`. Default is `None`. [node_attr_to]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["color"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute to write the colors to. Default is `"color"`, which the interactive graph widget uses to fill nodes. Any existing values in this attribute are overwritten for the colored nodes. [palette]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | list[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["default"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Either the name of a built-in palette or a list of color strings (e.g., `["#e41a1c", "#377eb8"]`). Built-in names include the ColorBrewer qualitative sets (`"Set1"`, `"Set2"`, `"Set3"`, `"Dark2"`, `"Paired"`, `"Accent"`, `"Pastel1"`, `"Pastel2"`), sequential and diverging ColorBrewer palettes (e.g., `"Greens"`, `"RdBu"`), the viridis family (`"viridis"`, `"magma"`, `"inferno"`, `"plasma"`, `"cividis"`), and `"default"`, `"vibrant"`, `"pastel"`, `"dark"`, and `"tableau"`. An unrecognized name raises a `ValueError`. Qualitative palettes are the best choice for unordered categories. [alpha]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Opacity as a percentage, from `0` (fully transparent) to `100` (opaque). When given, an alpha channel is appended to every color, giving `#RRGGBBAA` strings (`alpha=50` gives `80`). The palette colors must then be hex strings (`#RGB` or `#RRGGBB`). If `None` (default), colors are written as given by the palette. [nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[list[str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A list of node IDs or labels restricting which nodes are read from `node_attr_from=` and therefore colored. If `None` (the default), all nodes are considered. Ignored when `values=` is given. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If neither `node_attr_from=` nor `values=` is provided, `palette=` is an unknown name or an empty list, or `alpha=` is outside `0`-`100` or used with a color that isn't a hex string. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Any categorical attribute can drive the colors. The two distinct `type` values are sorted (`"organization"` before `"person"`) and given the first two `"tableau"` colors, so `A` and `B` share a color while `C` gets another: ::: {#f4db03a9 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec G = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes( {"A": {"type": "person"}, "B": {"type": "person"}, "C": {"type": "organization"}} ) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C")]) ) G.colorize_node_attrs(node_attr_from="type", palette="tableau") G.get_node_attrs("color") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {2: '#f28e2c', 3: '#4e79a7', 1: '#f28e2c'} ``` ::: ::: Detecting communities first and then colorizing by that attribute gives each community a visually distinct color: ::: {#2d51cf87 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} G = ec.Graph(directed=False) G.add_nodes(range(6)) # Two separate triangles G.add_edges([("0", "1"), ("1", "2"), ("0", "2"), ("3", "4"), ("4", "5"), ("3", "5")]) G.cmty_louvain(attr_name="community") G.colorize_node_attrs(node_attr_from="community", palette="Set1") G.get_node_df().select("label", "community", "color") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
shape: (6, 3)
labelcommunitycolor

"0"0"#e41a1c"
"1"0"#e41a1c"
"2"0"#e41a1c"
"3"1"#377eb8"
"4"1"#377eb8"
"5"1"#377eb8"
``` ::: ::: A plain list of colors can be passed instead of a named palette. Colors are assigned to the sorted values, so `"active"` gets the first color and `"inactive"` the second; writing to `node_attr_to="fill"` leaves any existing `color` attribute alone: ::: {#1c786a40 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} G = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A", status="inactive") .add_node(label="B", status="active") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") ) G.colorize_node_attrs( node_attr_from="status", palette=["#2ca02c", "#d62728"], node_attr_to="fill", ) G.get_node_attrs("fill") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {2: '#2ca02c', 1: '#d62728'} ``` ::: ::: A `values=` dict colors nodes by data that isn't stored on the graph. Keys can be labels, and nodes not in the dict (here `B`) are left uncolored: ::: {#d59bd877 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} G = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) G.colorize_node_attrs(values={"A": "north", "C": "south"}, palette="Dark2") G.get_node_attrs("color") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` {3: '#d95f02', 1: '#1b9e77'} ``` ::: ::: `alpha=` makes the colors semi-transparent by appending an alpha channel: ::: {#960ab744 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} G.colorize_node_attrs(values={"A": "north", "C": "south"}, palette="Dark2", alpha=50) G.get_node_attrs("color") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` {3: '#d95f0280', 1: '#1b9e7780'} ``` ::: :::
